subtask: Create a data dictionary describing coded outcomes, observation windows, and measurement units.

case_info.task_request: Create a data dictionary for the synthetic linked vaccination cohort, emphasizing outcome ascertainment, enrollment-based observation windows, and source-specific measurement units.
inputs: The linked extract contains 320 people with vaccination records, insurance enrollment intervals, and laboratory results.
The risk window runs from vaccination day 14 through day 180 inclusive, ending earlier at insurance disenrollment.
infection_status codes are 0=no qualifying positive test during observed time, 1=qualifying positive test, and 9=no observable risk days.
Example record: person_id=V088, vaccination_day=0, enrollment_end_day=90, positive_test_day=95; the test falls outside that person's observable window.
Laboratory source A reports CRP in mg/L; source B reports CRP in mg/dL; both retain source_unit and unconverted source_value.
Encounter counts represent distinct encounter IDs, not claim lines; one supplied encounter has four associated claim lines.

subtask: Create a data dictionary describing coded outcomes, observation windows, and measurement units.

case_info.task_request: Create a data dictionary for the synthetic kidney disease cohort, documenting repeated laboratory outcomes, specimen-selection windows, measurement units, and definitions still awaiting approval.
inputs: The cohort contains 110 people; index day 0 is the first nephrology consultation.
Baseline creatinine uses specimens from days -30 through 0; follow-up bins are days 1–90, 91–180, and 181–365, all inclusive.
Each bin selects the specimen closest to its final day; equal-distance ties select the later collection timestamp.
Example record: person_id=K027, specimen_day=176, creatinine=1.8 mg/dL, eGFR=38 mL/min/1.73 m², dialysis_status=0.
dialysis_status codes are 0=no documented dialysis, 1=maintenance dialysis, 2=temporary dialysis, and 9=status unknown; a bin with no specimen has laboratory values=null.
The proposed decline_outcome codes are 0=threshold not met, 1=threshold met, and 9=not assessable, but the investigator has not approved the percentage threshold or repeat-confirmation interval.

subtask: Build a query calculating data completeness by collection site and study period.

case_info.task_request: Build a PostgreSQL query calculating completeness of required enrollment fields by collection site and calendar quarter.
inputs: Synthetic table enrollment contains participant_id, site_id, enrolled_at, age_years, sex_code, and baseline_bp.
The study window is 2025-01-01 through 2025-06-30; quarters are assigned using enrolled_at.
Required fields are age_years, sex_code, and baseline_bp; NULL and blank sex_code count as missing, while age_years = 0 is valid.
Each participant has one enrollment row; report participant count, nonmissing count and percentage for each required field, and percentage with all three fields complete.
The research coordinator passes the query to the data analyst, who runs it against the synthetic extract and supplies site-quarter summaries to the study epidemiologist.

subtask: Build a query calculating data completeness by collection site and study period.

case_info.task_request: Build a SQL Server query measuring expected follow-up field completeness by collection site and study visit period, including missed visits.
inputs: Synthetic tables are expected_visits(participant_id, site_id, visit_period) and observed_visits(participant_id, visit_period, weight_kg, symptom_score).
Study periods are month_3 and month_6; expected_visits defines the denominator, including participants with no observed visit row.
There are 80 expected month_3 visits and 74 expected month_6 visits across sites East and West; observed_visits has at most one row per participant-period.
Example records: expected P201/East/month_3 has no observed row; P202/East/month_3 has weight_kg = 68.4 and symptom_score = NULL.
Both fields are required at each expected visit; symptom_score = 0 is complete, and absent visits contribute missing values for both fields.
The longitudinal data manager hands the query to the biostatistician, who uses field-level and fully complete visit percentages when planning missing-data handling.

subtask: Build a query calculating data completeness by collection site and study period.

case_info.task_request: Build a BigQuery query calculating eligibility-adjusted laboratory completeness by collection site and monthly study period.
inputs: Synthetic table lab_visits contains visit_id, site_id, visit_date, diabetes_flag, hba1c_value, creatinine_value, and creatinine_status.
Use visit_date to form monthly periods for July through September 2025; every row is a distinct attended visit.
HbA1c is required only when diabetes_flag = TRUE; creatinine is required for every visit.
Example rows: V301/Harbor/2025-07-09/FALSE/NULL/0.9/final; V302/Harbor/2025-07-10/TRUE/NULL/NULL/pending.
A creatinine result is complete only when its value is non-NULL and status is final; pending results remain incomplete at the extract cutoff of 2025-10-07.
The laboratory research lead supplies the query to the data engineer for execution; the engineer sends eligible denominators and completeness percentages to the clinical investigator.

subtask: Build a query calculating data completeness by collection site and study period.

case_info.task_request: Build a PostgreSQL query calculating questionnaire completeness by collection site and study wave after selecting the latest submitted revision.
inputs: Synthetic table questionnaire_revisions contains participant_id, site_id, wave, revision_id, submitted_at, q1, q2, and q3.
Study waves are baseline and annual; each participant belongs to one collection site, but a participant-wave may have multiple revisions.
Select the latest submitted_at per participant-wave, breaking timestamp ties with the greatest revision_id.
Example: P401/Central/baseline revision 1 has q1 = 2, q2 = 3, q3 = 1; revision 2 has q1 = 2, q2 = 99, q3 = 1.
All three items are required; NULL and code 99 mean missing, while codes 0 through 4 are complete. Report item-level and whole-questionnaire completeness using selected revisions only.
The survey methodologist passes the query to the research programmer; the programmer shares summaries with the site liaison for routine clarification of questionnaire coding.

subtask: Build a query calculating data completeness by collection site and study period.

case_info.task_request: Build a Snowflake query calculating completeness by collection site and protocol-defined study period, retaining periods with no records and identifying unmapped dates.
inputs: Synthetic tables are sites(site_id), study_periods(period_id, start_date, end_date), and encounters(encounter_id, site_id, encounter_date, diagnosis_code, encounter_type).
Sites are Ridge, Valley, and Lake; study periods are pilot [2025-01-01, 2025-02-15) and main [2025-03-01, 2025-06-01), with exclusive end dates.
Example encounters: E501/Ridge/2025-02-10/A12/outpatient; E502/Valley/2025-02-20/NULL/outpatient; E503/Ridge/2025-03-03/blank/NULL.
Lake has no encounters in either period; retain every site-period combination with record count 0 and completeness percentages NULL when the denominator is zero.
Both diagnosis_code and encounter_type are required; NULL and whitespace-only strings are missing. Dates outside all defined periods need a separate unmapped count by site.

The study data steward gives the query to the warehouse analyst; the analyst sends mapped completeness summaries to the epidemiologist and unmapped counts back to the steward for period-definition review.

The protocol defines baseline as days -14 through 0, early follow-up as days 1 through 30, and late follow-up as days 31 through 90, with inclusive boundaries.
Retain every measurement within its window rather than selecting one representative value; flag records outside all windows.

inputs: Synthetic records contain patient_id, encounter_id, admission_timestamp, discharge_timestamp, measurement_timestamp, and spo2_pct.
The supplied specification uses consecutive 24-hour windows beginning at admission; windows are left-closed and right-open, and measurements at discharge are excluded.
Encounter E17 runs from 2025-03-08T18:00:00-05:00 to 2025-03-10T12:00:00-04:00 and crosses a daylight-saving transition.
E17 measurements include 2025-03-09T17:59:00-04:00: 95 and 2025-03-09T19:00:00-04:00: 94; elapsed time must be evaluated in UTC.
One patient has two admissions three days apart; measurements must never be pooled across encounter_id values.

inputs: The synthetic extract contains participant_id, enrollment_date, specimen_date, lab_record_id, and hba1c_pct.
Target visits occur at days 90, 180, and 270 after enrollment; each accepts measurements within 60 days before or after its target.
A measurement eligible for multiple visits belongs only to the nearest target; an exact distance tie belongs to the earlier target.
Participant P22 has records L1 at day 135 with HbA1c 7.4, L2 at day 150 with 7.1, and L3 at day 330 with 6.9.
Preserve all measurements assigned to each visit; do not calculate means or select a single laboratory result.
The study coordinator has supplied the approved window rules; the analyst needs boundary and overlap tests before handing the function to the statistician.

case_info.task_request: Implement participant-local calendar-week grouping for wearable step measurements, retaining missingness and wear-time information.
inputs: Synthetic daily records contain participant_id, local_date, steps, and wear_minutes; enrollment dates and participant time zones are supplied separately.
Observation weeks run Monday through Sunday in each participant's local calendar; include the enrollment week but exclude daily records before enrollment.
Participant P08 enrolled Wednesday 2025-04-09; records include April 8: 6200 steps/700 wear minutes, April 9: 4300/480, and April 13: 0/0.
A day is valid when wear_minutes is at least 600; retain invalid days in their groups and label their validity without converting missing steps to zero.
Emit every observation week intersecting the participant's first 28 enrolled calendar days, including weeks with no recorded days.
Weekly groups must carry recorded-day and valid-day counts; no weekly step average is requested.

The current configuration defines pre-initiation as days -30 through -1 and follow-up as days 1 through 14; handling of day 0 is awaiting protocol approval.

Site B has a total study allocation of 80 participants and a capacity of 10 monthly, but enrolls nobody during September renovations.

case_info.task_request: Write a Python function that calculates bird observations per survey hour by species, wetland, and season, keeping missing counts distinct from zero.
inputs: Synthetic records contain wetland_id, season, species, count, and survey_minutes.
Example records: Marsh_A, spring, reed_warbler, 12, 40; Marsh_A, autumn, reed_warbler, 7, 30; Marsh_B, spring, reed_warbler, 0, 20.
Another record has Marsh_B, autumn, reed_warbler, a missing count, and 25 survey minutes.
Each survey lasts more than zero minutes; a missing count means the species tally was not submitted.
Habitat notes identify Marsh_A as reedbed and Marsh_B as open-water margin; these labels must remain available in the output.
The field technician supplies checked records to the monitoring coordinator, who passes the function to the wetland ecologist for seasonal comparisons.

subtask: Draft an explanation of how uneven survey coverage affects the provided trend estimates.

case_info.task_request: Draft an explanation of how the expanded stream survey network affects the provided mussel-population and suitable-habitat trends, keeping the original network distinct from newly added reaches.
inputs: Synthetic monitoring covered 15 established stream reaches in 2018; in 2024 it covered those same reaches plus 20 newly added tributary reaches.
The supplied network-wide mean falls from 8.0 to 5.6 mussels per quadrat, while the 15 established reaches average 8.3 mussels per quadrat in 2024.
Suitable substrate occurs in 72% of surveyed quadrats in 2018 and 51% in the expanded 2024 network; the established reaches record 70% in 2024.
New tributary reaches were selected to fill geographic gaps, not through random selection; 14 have finer sediment than any established reach.
Each reach received ten quadrats in both survey rounds, but no historical records exist for the new reaches.
The freshwater ecologist requests the explanation from records supplied by the database custodian; a catchment officer will use it when comparing restoration areas.

users.job_scope: Maintains reach histories and quadrat records.
Interprets mussel and stream-habitat monitoring trends.
Compares candidate areas for restoration assessment.

dependencies.use: Provides original-network and added-reach records.
Passes the explanation with separate network estimates for restoration comparisons.

First compute tray means for leaf area and height; then report treatment means and sample standard deviations across tray means, plus tray counts.
Return seedling counts within trays and treatment-level means for photon flux and temperature, weighting each tray equally.

Convert height to centimeters and temperature to degrees Celsius before summarizing.
Return valid counts, medians, and 25th and 75th percentiles for height, temperature, and conductivity in each species-treatment group.
Supplied invalid examples include height=-4 cm and height_unit=inch; flag these height values rather than silently converting or including them.
Keep valid environmental measurements from rows with invalid heights; return a separate issue table containing row_id and the affected field.

Expected coverage is one reading per hour; some windows have missing hours, and windows with no readings must retain the plant with missing exposure summaries.

Scores are 100 × recycled content/100, 100 × strength/600, and 100 × (5 − migration)/5, respectively; clamp scores to 0–100 and use mean measurements for nominal ranking.

subtask: Summarize associations between process deviations and recorded product quality measurements.

case_info.task_request: Summarize the associations between crystallization temperature deviations and recorded purity and particle-size measurements, distinguishing paired records from incomplete records.

Batches C03 and C04 exceeded the profile by 4 °C for 20 and 35 minutes; purity was 98.8% and 98.6%, and D50 was 92 and 85 µm.
C05 had a 3 °C excursion and purity of 99.0%, but its particle-size sample was lost; C06 has particle-size results pending.
Agitation stayed at 180 rpm for C01–C04; no microscopy results are available to assess crystal shape.

subtask: Summarize associations between process deviations and recorded product quality measurements.

case_info.task_request: Summarize how recorded neutralization deviations align with viscosity and residual-acidity measurements, keeping raw-material differences visible.
inputs: All records are synthetic; eight waterborne resin batches targeted endpoint pH 7.2–7.6 and neutralizer addition over 30 minutes.
R11 and R12 used feed lot A, reached pH 7.4 and 7.3, and had viscosities of 820 and 845 mPa·s with residual acidity of 0.08 and 0.09 mmol/g.
R13 and R14 used feed lot A, received neutralizer over 12 and 15 minutes, reached pH 8.0 and 7.9, and had viscosities of 1,040 and 1,010 mPa·s with residual acidity of 0.03 and 0.04 mmol/g.
R15 and R16 used feed lot B, followed the 30-minute addition, and had viscosities of 980 and 995 mPa·s at endpoint pH 7.4 and 7.5.
Feed lot B had an incoming acid value of 48 mg KOH/g versus 42 mg KOH/g for lot A; residual-acidity results for R15–R18 are pending.
Viscosity was measured at 25 °C; R17 and R18 lack recorded addition durations and should not be assigned to a deviation group.

Questions concern whether text reminders reduce missed appointments and whether effects differ between first and repeat visits.
Appointment fields include appointment_id, patient_id, clinic_id, reminder_sent, visit_type, scheduled_time, arrival_time, and status.
Example records: A102, P031, K1, yes, repeat, 09:00, 09:12, attended; A103, P031, K1, no, repeat, 14:00, null, canceled.
Statuses are attended, missed, or canceled; cancellation timestamps and reasons are unavailable, and reminder use was chosen by each clinic.
The operations analyst sends the checklist to the data steward for field validation and to the clinical evaluator for analysis planning.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an analysis checklist linking employee survey questions to available measurements, highlighting weighting requirements and questions the current data cannot support.
inputs: A synthetic workforce survey has 460 responses from 1,200 invited employees across office, warehouse, and field roles.
Questions concern overall job satisfaction, differences by work setting, and whether satisfaction changed since last year.
Current fields are anonymous_response_id, work_setting, tenure_band, satisfaction_1_to_5, and workload_1_to_5; 38 responses lack tenure_band.
Invitation counts are office 400, warehouse 500, and field 300; response counts are office 240, warehouse 150, and field 70.
Last year's extract contains only an overall mean satisfaction of 3.6 and 390 responses; respondent identifiers and work-setting totals were not retained.
The workforce researcher passes the checklist to the survey statistician, whose analysis specification goes to the HR planning partner.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an analysis checklist linking our packaging experiment questions to recorded measurements, emphasizing paired comparisons, batch structure, and measurement validation.
inputs: Synthetic experiment records cover 24 production batches; ten packages from each batch were tested with both the standard and revised seal settings.
Questions concern changes in seal strength, changes in leakage frequency, and variation across production batches.
Fields are batch_id, package_id, setting, test_order, seal_strength_N, leak_flag, and machine_id; package_id identifies paired measurements.
Example paired records: B07, P03, standard, 1, 42.1, 0, M2; B07, P03, revised, 2, 45.8, 0, M2.
Test order was randomized within batches; six seal-strength values were recorded as zero, and technician notes have not yet confirmed whether these represent failures or instrument errors.
The quality engineer sends the checklist to the laboratory technician for measurement checks and to the experimental statistician for analysis specification.

Plans paired and batch-aware comparisons.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an analysis checklist linking our stream-restoration questions to available measurements, emphasizing timing, site comparability, and pending data linkage.
inputs: Synthetic monitoring data cover eight restored stream sites and eight comparison sites, with monthly observations for 12 months before and 12 months after restoration.
Questions concern changes in nitrate concentration and whether changes vary with rainfall or upstream agricultural land cover.
Water records contain site_id, sample_date, nitrate_mg_L, water_temperature_C, and restoration_date; land-cover records contain site_id and agricultural_percent.
Rainfall is available as daily station totals from three gauges, but site-to-gauge assignments are pending; 22 of 384 planned water samples are missing because sites were inaccessible.
The watershed scientist passes the checklist to the GIS analyst for linkage work and to the environmental statistician for study-analysis planning.

users.job_scope: Defines restoration questions and maintains the monitoring inventory.
Links sites to rainfall gauges and verifies spatial covariates.
Plans longitudinal comparisons and evaluates site comparability.

Provides gauge assignments and linkage definitions for rainfall-adjusted analyses.

subtask: Calculate group mean differences and confidence intervals from supplied study measurements.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the mean within-person difference between workstation B and workstation A, with a 95% paired-t confidence interval.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the observed-case program-minus-comparison mean difference in weekly exercise minutes and a 95% Welch confidence interval, clearly identifying the missing-data limitation.
inputs: The synthetic study enrolled 50 adults in the program group and 48 in an independent comparison group.
At follow-up, the program group has 42 observed values, mean = 146 minutes, and sample standard deviation = 52 minutes.
The comparison group has 45 observed values, mean = 128 minutes, and sample standard deviation = 47 minutes.
Eight program values and three comparison values are missing; reasons and individual baseline measurements have not yet been supplied.
Use observed sample sizes for the interval, do not impute values, and distinguish the observed-case comparison from an estimate for all enrolled adults.
The evaluation officer sends the output to the program director for interpretation and to the field coordinator, who will collect missingness reasons for later sensitivity work.

subtask: Calculate group mean differences and confidence intervals from supplied study measurements.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the standardized treatment-minus-control mean difference across experience strata and its 95% normal-approximation confidence interval using the supplied fixed weights.
inputs: The synthetic study measures task accuracy on a 0–100 scale in independent treatment and control groups, stratified by prior experience.
Novice stratum: treatment n = 60, mean = 78, sample standard deviation = 10; control n = 80, mean = 73, sample standard deviation = 12.
Experienced stratum: treatment n = 90, mean = 91, sample standard deviation = 6; control n = 70, mean = 89, sample standard deviation = 7.
The target population weights are fixed at 0.40 novice and 0.60 experienced; apply these same weights to both groups rather than using observed group proportions.
All observations are complete and independent across groups and strata; combine stratum difference variances using squared weights and use 1.96 for the interval multiplier.
The workforce analyst requests the standardized comparison, then passes it to the operations lead, who needs an estimate aligned with the target workforce composition.

users.job_scope: Analyzes employee studies using target-population composition.
Uses workforce-adjusted study estimates to compare operational interventions.

dependencies.use: Provides the standardized mean difference and confidence interval for the target workforce.

case_info.task_request: Fit a linear regression comparing final test scores between tutoring groups, adjusting for baseline score and grade level; report the adjusted difference with a 95% confidence interval.

Students belong to 12 classrooms; account for classroom clustering when estimating uncertainty.
All scores and covariates are complete; use usual instruction as the reference group.

case_info.task_request: Fit a logistic regression comparing 30-day readmission between discharge pathways, adjusting for age, comorbidity score, and prior admissions; emphasize adjusted readmission probabilities.

Use standard discharge as the reference and calculate adjusted probabilities standardized to the supplied sample's covariate distribution.
Each discharge belongs to a different synthetic patient; pathway assignment was observational.

subtask: Fit a regression model comparing groups while adjusting for supplied covariates.

case_info.task_request: Fit a count regression comparing defect rates between machine types, adjusting for material grade and operator experience, with production volume as an exposure offset.
inputs: The synthetic dataset has 240 machine-shift records from 24 machines, evenly split between legacy and upgraded types.
Fields are machine_id, machine_type, material_grade, operator_experience_years, units_produced, and defects.
Example records: M01, legacy, B, 3, 1200, 18; M14, upgraded, A, 8, 950, 7.
Production volume ranges from 400 to 1800 units per shift, and every exposure value is positive.
Defect counts have an unadjusted mean of 11.4 and variance of 39.8; assess dispersion before choosing Poisson or negative binomial regression.
Use legacy machines as the reference, account for repeated shifts within machines, and report the adjusted rate ratio with a 95% confidence interval.

subtask: Fit a regression model comparing groups while adjusting for supplied covariates.

case_info.task_request: Fit a mixed-effects regression comparing monthly satisfaction trajectories between onboarding groups, adjusting for tenure and job family; estimate group differences at months 1, 3, and 6.

Satisfaction is measured on a 0–100 scale at months 1, 3, and 6; 267 of 288 planned observations are available.
Example records: E001, coached, 1, 2, technical, 74; E001, coached, 3, 2, technical, 81; field order is employee_id, group, month, prior_tenure_years, job_family, satisfaction.
Supplied baseline covariates are prior tenure in years and job family, coded technical, administrative, or customer service.
Use categorical month, a group-by-month interaction, and an employee random intercept.
Reasons for the 21 missing observations are recorded as leave or nonresponse; use observed outcomes and state the missingness assumption.

case_info.task_request: Rewrite the explanation of Python loop accumulation in short steps using the learner's experience totaling spreadsheet rows.
inputs: The adult learner can use SUM in a spreadsheet but has completed only one introductory Python session.
The supplied code is: total = 0; then for price in [4, 7, 2]: total = total + price; then print(total).
The original explanation says: 'The accumulator updates its state on each iteration over the iterable.'
The learner asked whether total = total + price is an equation that must already be true.
Avoid 'accumulator,' 'iteration,' and 'iterable' until after their plain-language meanings; show one loop pass at a time.

case_info.task_request: Rewrite the water-cycle explanation in short steps using the learner's observations of drying clothes and cold glasses.
inputs: The grade 6 learner is developing English proficiency and understands everyday words such as wet, dry, warm, and cold.
The original explanation says: 'Solar energy drives evaporation, followed by condensation and precipitation as water circulates through Earth's systems.'
The learner described wet clothes becoming dry and droplets appearing outside a cold glass.
During a vocabulary check, the learner matched rain to precipitation but confused evaporation with condensation.
Keep each step to one sentence of no more than 12 words; retain the three scientific terms with brief everyday definitions.

inputs: The grade 9 learner can retell events in order but treats the last event before a change as its only cause.

Use the school example before introducing 'long-term condition' and 'immediate trigger'; do not add historical events not supplied.

inputs: The apprentice plumber is taking a basic electrical theory module and understands pressure, flow rate, and narrow pipes.

The apprentice said, 'A resistor must store current like a tank stores water.'
Use at most six steps, introduce voltage, current, and resistance separately, and explicitly avoid the storage misconception.
The vocational tutor will check the rewrite with the electrical instructor, then give the approved version to the workshop coach for a desk-based review.

Learner A wrote 24 ÷ 8 = 3 g/cm³ for Block P; Learner B wrote 15 ÷ 30 = 0.5 g/cm³ for Block Q.
Both learners practiced reading volume marks on a drawing of a graduated cylinder; A recorded 18 mL and B recorded 20 mL for the same drawing.
A asked whether a larger object must be denser; B asked why density uses division. Neither question received a recorded explanation.

inputs: The synthetic Grade 8 investigation used 12 bean plants per group over 14 days.
Group A received 4 hours of light daily and grew a mean of 3.2 cm; Group B received 8 hours and grew 5.6 cm; Group C received 12 hours and grew 5.8 cm.
All groups used the same soil and pot size, but watering amounts were not recorded.

Source A: a fictional 1892 council notice states, 'The new water line serves all six central streets; outer wards will be considered next year.'
Source B: a fictional 1892 resident letter states, 'Our outer-ward households still carry water from the pump, while central shops have taps.'
Source C: a fictional 1893 municipal ledger lists 180 connected central properties and 20 connected outer-ward properties, without total property counts.

Use one sourcing question, one corroboration question, and two inference questions; each response must cite an excerpt and fit within 80 words.

subtask: Create annotated sample responses illustrating the levels in a supplied rubric.

case_info.task_request: Create annotated sample responses at all four supplied history rubric levels, making source evaluation visible without requiring outside historical knowledge.
inputs: All materials are fictional: students compare two accounts of a town's 1912 school opening and answer, 'What can these sources establish about community support for the school?'

Source A is a mayor's opening-day speech stating, 'Every household welcomes this school'; Source B is a private letter written two days later by a shopkeeper stating, 'Several neighbors object to the new school tax, though the hall was crowded.'

Rubric: Level 4 compares both sources, evaluates their purposes or positions, and makes a qualified conclusion; Level 3 compares both sources and makes a supported conclusion but offers limited source evaluation; Level 2 uses one source accurately or juxtaposes both without a supported comparison; Level 1 misreads the sources or makes unsupported assertions.
Create one 100–140-word response per level; each annotation must identify source use, evaluation, and the basis for the assigned level.
The rubric is approved, but no anchor responses exist yet; mark every sample as proposed and avoid claims about actual town opinion beyond the supplied excerpts.
The history teacher submits the samples to the curriculum specialist for alignment review; the specialist passes approved examples to the moderation lead for a grading workshop.

inputs: Synthetic circuit values: series resistor R = 3.3 kΩ, shunt capacitor C = 47 nF, and installed load RL = 10 kΩ in parallel with C.
Use H(s) = RL / (R + RL + s R RL C) for the loaded circuit and H(s) = 1 / (1 + s R C) for the open-circuit output.
The source is ideal; plot Vout/Vin from 10 Hz to 100 kHz with a logarithmic frequency axis.
Show magnitude in dB and phase in degrees, with separately labeled traces for both load conditions.
The analog designer sends the plots to the interface engineer, who uses them when selecting the input impedance of the next stage.

subtask: Plot a filter's frequency response using supplied component values and circuit equations.

case_info.task_request: Plot the RC high-pass filter's theoretical magnitude response and overlay the supplied bench measurements without fitting the component values.
inputs: Synthetic circuit values: series capacitor C = 100 nF and shunt resistor R = 22 kΩ; output is measured across R.
Use H(s) = s R C / (1 + s R C), with s = j 2πf; neglect source resistance and oscilloscope loading.
Synthetic bench records list frequency, input RMS voltage, and output RMS voltage: 20 Hz, 1.00 V, 0.26 V; 100 Hz, 1.00 V, 0.79 V; 1 kHz, 1.00 V, 0.98 V.
Plot 5 Hz to 10 kHz on a logarithmic frequency axis; convert measured voltage ratios to dB and retain the individual measurement markers.

subtask: Plot a filter's frequency response using supplied component values and circuit equations.

case_info.task_request: Plot the equal-component Sallen–Key low-pass response for both proposed gain-resistor options, emphasizing passband shape.
inputs: Synthetic filter values: R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ and C1 = C2 = 10 nF.
Use H(s) = K / ((s R C)^2 + (3 - K) s R C + 1), where R = R1, C = C1, and K = 1 + Rf/Rg.
Both options use Rg = 10 kΩ; option A uses Rf = 5.6 kΩ and option B uses Rf = 8.2 kΩ.
Assume an ideal op-amp; plot 10 Hz to 100 kHz and include both absolute magnitude in dB and magnitude normalized to each option's DC gain.

case_info.task_request: Plot the two-stage RC low-pass response with and without an ideal interstage buffer, using the supplied equations and matching plot scales.
inputs: Synthetic ladder values: R1 = 4.7 kΩ, C1 = 22 nF, R2 = 10 kΩ, and C2 = 10 nF; each capacitor connects its stage output to ground.
For the unbuffered ladder, use H(s) = 1 / (1 + s(R1 C1 + R1 C2 + R2 C2) + s² R1 R2 C1 C2).
For an ideal unity-gain buffer between the stages, use H(s) = 1 / ((1 + s R1 C1)(1 + s R2 C2)).

subtask: Prepare a timing diagram from supplied signal transitions and interface specifications.

inputs: The synthetic capture covers a controller addressing a temperature sensor on an open-drain I2C bus; both lines start high.
SDA falls at 0 us while SCL is high; SCL falls at 2 us, and the first eight SCL rising edges occur at 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, and 75 us.
Each of the first eight SCL high intervals lasts 4 us; SDA values at their rising edges are 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, and 0, with each value established 2 us beforehand.
For the ninth clock, the controller releases SCL at 85 us, but the sensor holds it low until 92 us; SCL crosses the high threshold at 92.6 us and falls at 96 us.
The controller releases SDA at 81 us; the sensor pulls it low at 83 us for acknowledgment and releases it at 97 us.
Pull-up rises take 0.6 us to reach the high threshold; the supplied interface limits require data setup of at least 0.25 us and SCL high time of at least 4 us.

DATA becomes 0x3A at 20 ns and changes at 40 ns to a payload whose value was not retained in the supplied record.
The source specification requires VALID and DATA to remain stable while VALID is high and READY is low; reset deassertion has no additional recovery constraint in this simulation.

RX stays high through the capture end at 195 us; there are no recorded transitions between the listed events.

The receiver model detects the start edge, checks the start bit after half a nominal bit period, then samples each data bit and the stop bit at one-bit intervals; oscillator error is excluded from this case.

The memory image contains 0xA6 at 0x0120 and 0x59 at 0x0121; the controller samples the data bus at 70 ns and 145 ns.

Batch L12: sample count 20, mean 30.018, sample standard deviation 0.015, minimum 29.987, maximum 30.047.
Batch L13: sample count 12, mean 30.006, sample standard deviation 0.009, minimum 29.989, maximum 30.023.
Only these rounded summaries are available; weight the overall mean by sample count and distinguish pooled within-batch variation from total variation including batch-mean differences.
The manufacturing analyst supplies the calculations to the quality manager, who uses them to decide whether to request raw records; capability claims require additional process-stability evidence.

A manual pilot of 500 initial assemblies produced 460 first-pass passes; 30 of the 40 failures passed rework and 10 were scrapped.

An automated pilot of 500 initial assemblies produced 485 first-pass passes; 12 of the 15 failures passed rework and 3 were scrapped.

Both routes require $0.40 deburring per unit; allocate each variant's setup costs to its own volume and report both variant-level and volume-weighted family unit costs.

inputs: The intake folder contains 18 invoice PDFs and a spreadsheet of 12 invoices already entered this month.
Invoice SYN-104 from Alder Office Supply totals $486.20; the same vendor, invoice number, and amount appear in the entered-invoice spreadsheet.
Invoice SYN-117 from Beacon Cleaning totals $720.00 and covers one month of office cleaning.
Approved categories are office supplies, cleaning services, utilities, and professional fees.
Each register entry must retain the source filename, invoice number, vendor, invoice date, total, category, and duplicate-review status.

users.job_scope: Collects incoming invoices and prepares entries for review.
Reviews classifications and resolves suspected duplicate entries.
Schedules payment of approved invoice entries.

dependencies.use: Provides the invoice register and linked sources for classification and duplicate review.
Passes approved entries and resolved duplicate statuses for payment scheduling.

subtask: Construct an invoice register linking source documents to expense categories.

case_info.task_request: Construct an invoice register with line-level expense categories and department allocations for the supplied mixed-purpose invoices.
inputs: Six invoices contain purchases shared by the sales and engineering departments.
Invoice SYN-208 includes $360.00 of printer paper for sales and $1,240.00 of monitor accessories for engineering.
Invoice SYN-211 charges $900.00 for shared internet service; the approved allocation is 40% sales and 60% engineering.
Approved categories are office consumables, computer peripherals, and telecommunications; all amounts are tax-exclusive, with no additional tax shown.
Entries must link to the source filename and page and retain both the invoice total and allocated line amounts.

users.job_scope: Prepares expense classifications and departmental allocations.
Checks expense ownership and allocation bases for both departments.
Posts approved expense allocations to departmental accounts.

dependencies.use: Sends source-linked allocations for departmental validation.
Provides validated allocation amounts and categories for posting.

subtask: Construct an invoice register linking source documents to expense categories.

case_info.task_request: Construct an invoice register linking each document to an expense category, keeping unsupported classifications pending rather than guessing.
inputs: The intake contains nine emailed invoices, three scanned receipts, and purchasing notes for five transactions.
Invoice SYN-302 from Cedar Services totals $1,850.00 and describes only 'monthly support'; no contract or purchase order is supplied.
Receipt SYN-R14 totals $92.40 and clearly lists envelopes and postage labels.
Invoice SYN-309 totals $640.00 for equipment maintenance and references purchase order PO-SYN-44, which is absent from the intake.
Approved categories are office supplies, postage, equipment maintenance, and IT support; missing evidence must be recorded alongside the source link.
Two scanned receipts have unreadable vendor names, although their dates and totals are legible.

users.job_scope: Registers incoming expense documents and records evidence gaps.
Retrieves purchase orders and clarifies vendor service descriptions.
Approves supported classifications and holds unresolved entries.

dependencies.use: Shares pending entries and source references to obtain missing purchasing evidence.
Supplies recovered documents and clarifications for classification approval.
Provides the register so supported entries can be reviewed separately from unresolved items.

subtask: Construct an invoice register linking source documents to expense categories.

case_info.task_request: Construct an invoice register linking invoices and credit notes to expense categories, preserving original amounts, currencies, and related-document references.
inputs: The supplied batch contains seven invoices and two credit notes in USD and EUR.
Invoice SYN-401 from Harbor Software is EUR 600.00 for a monthly subscription; the supplied accounting rate is USD 1.10 per EUR.
Credit note SYN-C09 is EUR 100.00 and explicitly references invoice SYN-401.
Invoice SYN-405 from Meadow Freight is USD 275.00 for delivery services.
Approved categories are software subscriptions and freight; credit notes must retain negative amounts and links to both their own files and referenced invoices.
Credit note SYN-C12 is USD 80.00 for a freight adjustment, but its referenced invoice SYN-388 is not supplied.

users.job_scope: Registers foreign-currency invoices and related supplier credits.
Reviews currency conversions, credit links, and expense classifications.
Obtains missing supplier documents and confirms credits available for settlement.

dependencies.use: Provides source-linked amounts and currency details for accounting review.
Provides unmatched credit references for supplier follow-up.
Supplies recovered invoices and credit confirmations to complete review.

subtask: Construct an invoice register linking source documents to expense categories.

case_info.task_request: Construct an invoice register linking incoming invoices to expense categories and service periods, and distinguish current expenses from items requiring prepaid review.
inputs: The month-end intake contains 11 invoices received in June, including services spanning more than one accounting period.
Invoice SYN-501 totals $2,400.00 for insurance coverage from July 1 through June 30 of the following year.
Invoice SYN-506 totals $450.00 for cleaning performed during June.
Invoice SYN-510 totals $1,200.00 for a software subscription, but the service start and end dates are not stated.
Approved expense categories are insurance, cleaning services, and software subscriptions; prepaid treatment requires reviewer approval.
Each entry must retain the source filename, receipt date, invoice date, amount, stated service period, expense category, and review status.

users.job_scope: Organizes invoice intake and identifies period-related accounting questions.
Approves expense timing and prepaid treatment.
Posts approved expenses and maintains prepaid schedules.

dependencies.use: Provides the categorized register and source-linked service periods for timing review.
Passes approved timing decisions for ledger posting and prepaid schedule maintenance.

subtask: Compare expense coding across recurring invoices and identify changed classifications.

case_info.task_request: Compare coding on recurring software invoices before and after the ledger migration, and flag classification changes for controller review.
inputs: The supplied extract covers six monthly invoices from fictional vendor Cedar Software, January–June 2025, at $840 each.
January–March records show GL 6100, Software subscriptions, and cost center OPS; April–June show GL 6250, IT services, and cost center OPS.
The accounting system migrated on April 1; the approved crosswalk maps old GL 6100 to new GL 7100, Software subscriptions.
Invoice descriptions and subscription quantities are unchanged across all six records.
The migration analyst supplied the crosswalk; the controller will review flagged differences before approving any recoding.

users.job_scope: Checks recurring invoice coding and prepares review items.
Maintains account mappings between the old and new systems.
Approves classification corrections and migration exceptions.

dependencies.use: Provides the approved account crosswalk for comparison.
Passes flagged coding changes for approval before recoding.

subtask: Compare expense coding across recurring invoices and identify changed classifications.

case_info.task_request: Compare line-level classifications on recurring facilities invoices, distinguishing coding changes from changes in the services billed.
inputs: Three supplied invoices from fictional vendor Harbor Facilities cover July–September 2025.
July contains cleaning, $1,200 to GL 6300 Janitorial, and waste collection, $300 to GL 6310 Waste services.
August contains cleaning, $1,200 to GL 6300, waste collection, $300 to GL 6300, and carpet restoration, $450 to GL 6320 Repairs.
September contains cleaning, $1,200 to GL 6300, and waste collection, $300 to GL 6310; carpet restoration does not recur.
The facilities coordinator confirms that carpet restoration was a one-time service; the AP supervisor reviews coding questions, while the coordinator receives service-description questions.

users.job_scope: Compares invoice lines and routes classification questions.
Verifies services performed and explains billing changes.
Reviews expense-account consistency and authorizes corrections.

dependencies.use: Supplies service context for comparing recurring lines.
Returns unresolved service-description questions for clarification.
Sends classification-change candidates for coding review.

subtask: Compare expense coding across recurring invoices and identify changed classifications.

case_info.task_request: Compare recurring consulting invoice allocations and identify changed classifications, showing which changes have approval evidence.
inputs: Four supplied invoices from fictional vendor Summit Advisory cover January–April 2025 at $10,000 per month.
January and February are coded entirely to GL 6400 Consulting, cost center CORP.
March is split $6,000 to GL 6400/CORP and $4,000 to GL 1505 Software implementation/CAPEX.
April is split $5,000 to GL 6400/CORP and $5,000 to GL 1505/CAPEX.
A supplied March approval authorizes a 40% implementation allocation; no April allocation approval is included.
The project manager supplies work-breakdown support, and the fixed-asset accountant uses the comparison to request missing evidence before posting adjustments.

users.job_scope: Checks recurring expense allocations against supporting approvals.
Documents project activities and proposed allocation percentages.
Reviews capitalization support and prepares approved adjustments.

dependencies.use: Provides work-breakdown records and allocation approvals.
Passes the coding comparison and approval gaps for follow-up.
Requests missing allocation evidence before adjustment preparation.

subtask: Compare expense coding across recurring invoices and identify changed classifications.

case_info.task_request: Compare recurring telecom expense coding across the department reorganization, separating approved department changes from other classification changes.
inputs: The supplied records contain February–May 2025 invoices from fictional vendor Valley Telecom for account VT-204, each totaling $2,400.
February and March use GL 6500 Telecommunications, department SALES, and location NORTH.
April uses GL 6500 Telecommunications, department CUSTOMER-OPS, and location NORTH.
May uses GL 6510 Data hosting, department CUSTOMER-OPS, and location NORTH.
An approved reorganization notice transfers account VT-204 from SALES to CUSTOMER-OPS effective April 1; it specifies no GL-account change.
The management accountant passes the comparison to the budget owner to validate ownership and to the GL accountant to review account coding.

users.job_scope: Reconciles recurring expense classifications with organizational changes.
Confirms departmental ownership of transferred expenses.
Reviews account classifications and posts approved corrections.

dependencies.use: Provides department-change comparisons for ownership validation.
Provides GL-account changes for separate classification review.

subtask: Compare expense coding across recurring invoices and identify changed classifications.

case_info.task_request: Compare the available recurring insurance records, flag changed expense classifications, and identify comparisons that need additional source records.
inputs: The supplied ledger extract contains fictional vendor Elm Insurance records for January, February, April, and May 2025; March is absent.
January invoice EI-101 and February invoice EI-102 each show $900 to GL 6600 Insurance, department ADMIN.
April invoice EI-104 shows $900 to GL 6610 Professional fees, department ADMIN.
May invoice EI-105 shows $900 to GL 6600 Insurance, department ADMIN, plus credit EI-C105 for -$900 to GL 6610 referencing EI-104.
Invoice PDFs are supplied only for January and May; May describes monthly liability coverage and labels the credit a coding correction.
The AP clerk retrieves missing records after the senior accountant's comparison; the close reviewer assesses resolved items once supporting records are added.

users.job_scope: Compares recurring classifications and tracks evidence gaps.
Retrieves invoice PDFs and missing ledger records.
Reviews supported coding changes and remaining open items.

dependencies.use: Sends specific missing-record requests from the comparison.
Returns retrieved records for completion of the comparison.
Passes supported comparisons and unresolved gaps for close review.

subtask: Calculate invoice aging bands from due dates and recorded payment dates.

case_info.task_request: Calculate aging bands for open customer invoices at March month-end, excluding invoices fully paid by the cutoff.
inputs: The synthetic receivables extract has a cutoff of 2025-03-31; include recorded payments dated on or before that day.
Use days past due: current at 0 or fewer days, then 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91+ days.
Invoice INV-101 is $4,800, due 2025-02-14, with no recorded payments.
Invoice INV-102 is $2,100, due 2025-03-31, with no recorded payments; INV-103 is $900, due 2025-04-15, with no recorded payments.
Invoice INV-104 is $3,200, due 2025-01-20, with a full $3,200 payment recorded on 2025-03-28.
The receivables clerk supplies the extract to the accounting analyst; the collections coordinator uses the analyst's work to prepare routine customer follow-ups.

users.job_scope: Maintain invoice records and recorded customer payments.
Calculate month-end outstanding balances and aging bands.
Prepare routine follow-ups for unpaid customer invoices.

dependencies.use: Provide the invoice and payment extract for aging.
Supply open-invoice aging for customer follow-up preparation.

subtask: Calculate invoice aging bands from due dates and recorded payment dates.

case_info.task_request: Reconstruct invoice aging at the June cutoff using partial payments, separating payments received after the cutoff.
inputs: The synthetic ledger was exported on 2025-07-10, but the requested aging date is 2025-06-30.
Use current for 0 or fewer days past due, followed by 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91+ days; age the remaining balance from the invoice due date.
Invoice INV-201 is $12,000, due 2025-04-30; allocated payments are $3,000 dated 2025-05-15 and $4,000 dated 2025-07-03.
Invoice INV-202 is $7,500, due 2025-06-15; an allocated payment of $2,500 is dated 2025-06-30.
The ledger's recorded payment date is the cash receipt date; payments after 2025-06-30 must not reduce the cutoff balance.
The controller requests the reconstruction and passes it to the financial reporting accountant, who uses it for the June receivables reconciliation.

users.job_scope: Oversee month-end accounting and approve historical cutoff treatment.
Reconcile June receivables to the closing ledger.

dependencies.use: Provide reconstructed cutoff aging for the June reconciliation.

subtask: Calculate invoice aging bands from due dates and recorded payment dates.

case_info.task_request: Calculate aging for allocated invoice balances and identify payment records that need reconciliation without assuming allocations.
inputs: Use synthetic records as of 2025-08-31 and bands of current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91+ days past due.
Customer C-301 has INV-301 for $5,000 due 2025-07-01 and INV-302 for $2,000 due 2025-08-20.
Receipt R-301 is $3,000 dated 2025-08-25 for C-301, but its invoice allocation field is blank.
Customer C-302 has INV-303 for $4,000 due 2025-06-30; receipt R-302 for $1,000 is allocated to it, but the payment date is blank.
Do not subtract unallocated cash from individual invoices; do not assume an undated payment occurred before the cutoff.
The cash application specialist requests preliminary aging, then sends unresolved records to the receivables supervisor; the supervisor supplies confirmed corrections to the collections analyst.

users.job_scope: Match customer receipts to invoices and identify incomplete payment records.
Resolve allocation and payment-date exceptions.
Use reconciled aging to plan customer account reviews.

dependencies.use: Submit preliminary aging and payment exceptions for reconciliation.
Pass confirmed corrections and reconciled balances for account reviews.

subtask: Calculate invoice aging bands from due dates and recorded payment dates.

case_info.task_request: Calculate invoice aging using approved due-date changes, keeping pending extensions and disputed balances separately identifiable.
inputs: The synthetic account review cutoff is 2025-09-30; use current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91+ days past due.
INV-401 is $8,000, originally due 2025-08-01; an approved amendment dated 2025-08-20 changes its due date to 2025-10-15.
INV-402 is $6,000, due 2025-08-15; a requested extension to 2025-10-31 is pending approval and must not replace the recorded due date.
INV-402 has an allocated $1,500 payment dated 2025-09-10 and a disputed $2,000 portion; no credit memo has been approved.
Disputed amounts remain in outstanding receivables and retain the invoice's aging band.
The credit analyst supplies amendment status to the receivables accountant; the accountant's aging goes to the account manager for customer discussions.

users.job_scope: Verify approved payment-term amendments and track pending extension requests.
Maintain outstanding invoice aging and distinguish disputed balances.
Discuss payment schedules and invoice disputes with customers.

dependencies.use: Provide approved and pending due-date amendment status.
Supply aging with extension and dispute flags for customer discussions.

subtask: Calculate invoice aging bands from due dates and recorded payment dates.

case_info.task_request: Calculate invoice aging in each invoice's currency, applying recorded payments and approved credits without combining currencies.
inputs: Use synthetic balances as of 2025-12-31 and bands of current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91+ days past due.
INV-501 is EUR 10,000, due 2025-10-31; an allocated EUR 4,000 payment is dated 2025-12-05.
An approved EUR 1,000 credit memo dated 2025-12-20 is allocated to INV-501 and reduces its outstanding balance.
INV-502 is USD 8,000, due 2025-12-15; an allocated USD 2,000 payment is dated 2026-01-02.
No exchange rates are supplied; retain separate EUR and USD aging totals, and exclude payments dated after the cutoff.
The regional accountant requests currency-specific aging; treasury uses it for cash planning, while the consolidation accountant later adds reporting-currency conversion using approved rates.

users.job_scope: Maintain original-currency receivables and year-end aging.
Plan expected customer cash receipts by currency.
Convert approved local-currency balances for group reporting.

dependencies.use: Provide separate currency aging totals for cash planning.
Provide original-currency aging for later conversion with approved rates.

subtask: Join customer receipts to invoice records using reference numbers and amounts.

case_info.task_request: Match the supplied customer receipts to invoices by reference number and amount, keeping reused references separate by customer account.
inputs: All records are synthetic and denominated in USD.
Invoice records include customer C101, reference INV-220, amount $840; customer C205, reference INV-220, amount $840; and customer C101, reference INV-221, amount $315.
Receipt R501 shows customer C101, reference INV-220, and amount $840.
Receipt R502 shows reference INV-220 and amount $840, but its customer account is blank.
The supplied bank payer details are unavailable; ambiguous receipts must remain pending rather than be assigned by amount alone.

users.job_scope: Prepares receipt-to-invoice matching work for customer accounts.
Reviews proposed matches and posts supported receipt allocations.
Obtains missing payer identification for unresolved receipts.

dependencies.use: Uses the matching work to review allocations before posting.
Passes unidentified receipts for customer clarification.

subtask: Join customer receipts to invoice records using reference numbers and amounts.

case_info.task_request: Join the batch receipts to the referenced invoices, separating partial payments from payments covering multiple invoices and retaining unpaid balances.
inputs: All records are synthetic and denominated in USD for customer C310.
Invoices INV-701, INV-702, and INV-703 have original amounts of $1,200, $450, and $650 respectively, with no prior allocations.
Receipt R610 is $500 and carries reference INV-701.
Receipt R611 is $1,100; its remittance lists INV-702 for $450 and INV-703 for $650.
The invoice export contains one row per invoice, while the remittance export contains one row per allocation; receipt totals must not be duplicated across joined rows.

users.job_scope: Reconciles receipt totals with invoice-level remittance allocations.
Uses remaining customer balances to plan routine payment follow-up.

dependencies.use: Provides reviewed allocations and remaining balances for follow-up.

subtask: Join customer receipts to invoice records using reference numbers and amounts.

case_info.task_request: Match receipts with shortened or missing invoice references using the supplied reference rules and amounts, distinguishing supported matches from items needing clarification.
inputs: All records are synthetic and denominated in GBP for customer C420.
Invoice records are INV-008142 for £275, INV-008143 for £410, and INV-008144 for £410.
Receipt R720 carries reference 8142 and amount £275.
Receipt R721 has a blank reference and amount £410; receipt R722 carries reference INV008143 and amount £410.
Approved normalization removes the INV prefix, hyphens, and leading zeros; amount-only matching is not approved.
The supplied receipt export covers one bank day, and no remittance advice has yet been obtained for R721.

users.job_scope: Applies approved reference normalization to imported receipts.
Requests remittance details from customer accounting contacts.
Approves supported matches and reviews unresolved allocation exceptions.

dependencies.use: Provides unresolved receipt details for remittance requests.
Provides normalized-reference matching work for approval.
Supplies customer clarification for exception review.

subtask: Join customer receipts to invoice records using reference numbers and amounts.

case_info.task_request: Join net customer receipts to invoices using references and supplied deduction details, without treating unexplained shortfalls as cleared receivables.
inputs: All records are synthetic and denominated in EUR.
Customer C530 invoice INV-910 is €2,000; receipt R830 references INV-910 and has a bank amount of €1,985.
The supplied bank advice for R830 identifies a €15 transfer fee deducted from a €2,000 customer payment.
Customer C540 invoice INV-911 is €1,250; receipt R831 references INV-911 and has a bank amount of €1,200.
The remittance for R831 claims a €50 pricing deduction, but no approved credit note is present.
Policy requires fee evidence for gross-payment reconciliation and billing approval before a customer deduction reduces the receivable.

users.job_scope: Matches receipts and distinguishes bank fees from customer deductions.
Checks pricing claims and authorizes valid credit adjustments.
Reviews open balances and approves reconciled receipt treatment.

dependencies.use: Passes unsupported customer deductions for billing review.
Provides receipt matches and supporting fee evidence for review.
Provides deduction approval or rejection before balance adjustments.

subtask: Join customer receipts to invoice records using reference numbers and amounts.

case_info.task_request: Join the receipt events to invoices by reference and amount, accounting for reversals and duplicate imports before updating outstanding receivables.
inputs: All records are synthetic and denominated in USD for customer C650.
Invoice INV-1201 is $900 and invoice INV-1202 is $600; both had no allocations before this batch.
Receipt event E901 records transaction TX88, reference INV-1201, and amount +$900.
Event E902 records transaction TX88-R, reference INV-1201, and amount -$900; its reversal_of field identifies TX88.
Events E903 and E904 both record transaction TX89, reference INV-1202, and amount +$600; they came from separate imports of the same bank file.
Bank transaction ID is the deduplication key; event IDs identify import rows, and the batch has not yet been posted.

users.job_scope: Reviews imported receipt events against invoice balances.
Corrects duplicate import rows while preserving the audit trail.
Posts approved receipt and reversal events to customer accounts.

dependencies.use: Provides duplicate-event details for import correction.
Provides invoice joins and reversal relationships for posting review.
Confirms corrected import rows before the batch is posted.

subtask: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an outstanding-balance table as of May 31, separating invoices, credits, and partial payments and grouping balances by customer and due-date band.
inputs: The May ledger lists Cedar Works invoice INV-401 for $8,400, due May 15, and invoice INV-418 for $2,100, due June 15.
Credit memo CM-77 for $600 is posted against INV-401; receipt PAY-92 for $3,000 is also allocated to INV-401.
Harbor Supply invoice INV-409 is $4,750, due May 25, with no recorded credits or payments.
Use due-date bands of not yet due, 1–30 days overdue, and more than 30 days overdue; all amounts are USD.
The receivables clerk supplies the ledger to the accounting supervisor, who passes the resulting table to the collections coordinator for routine customer follow-up.

users.job_scope: Reviews month-end customer balances and requests receivables summaries.
Maintains invoice, credit, and cash-allocation records.
Uses approved balances to plan routine customer follow-up.

dependencies.use: Supplies the month-end ledger and transaction allocations.
Provides the reviewed outstanding-balance table for follow-up planning.

subtask: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments, with unapplied cash and unresolved allocations shown separately.
inputs: The supplied ledger shows Maple Clinic invoices INV-510 for $6,000 and INV-511 for $2,500, both due July 10.
Receipt RC-204 for $2,000 is explicitly allocated to INV-510.
A second Maple Clinic receipt, RC-209 for $1,800, has no invoice reference or allocation record.
Credit memo CM-105 for $450 references INV-511 and is posted; a bank deposit of $900 has payer text 'MAPLE' but no confirmed customer match.
The cash-application specialist provides receipt details to the receivables analyst; the analyst sends the table to the finance manager for review of unresolved items.
Use only confirmed allocations to reduce invoice balances; do not assign the unidentified deposit to a customer.

users.job_scope: Reconciles customer balances and identifies allocation gaps.
Matches bank receipts to customers and invoices.
Reviews balance reconciliations and assigns unresolved cash items.

dependencies.use: Provides confirmed receipt allocations and unmatched deposit details.
Provides the table so unresolved allocations can be reviewed and assigned.

subtask: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments, and distinguish posted credits from pending dispute adjustments.
inputs: Northgate Retail invoice INV-620 totals $12,000 and was due August 20; a $5,000 partial payment is allocated to it.
Posted credit memo CM-142 reduces INV-620 by $800 for returned goods.
The customer disputes another $1,200 on INV-620; the account manager has submitted a credit request, but accounting has not approved or posted it.
Invoice INV-633 for the same customer totals $3,400, is due September 20, and has no recorded payments or credits.
The account manager supplies dispute notes to the billing accountant, who sends the table to both the credit controller and the account manager.
Keep the pending $1,200 adjustment visible without treating it as a posted credit; the credit controller uses posted balances for collection decisions.

users.job_scope: Maintains billed receivables and verifies posted credit adjustments.
Documents customer disputes and coordinates commercial resolutions.
Reviews collectible balances and approves collection actions.

dependencies.use: Supplies dispute details and the pending credit request.
Provides posted balances and separately identified disputed adjustments.
Provides the same table for customer discussions about the disputed charge.

subtask: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an outstanding-balance table for the September close, separating invoices, credits, and partial payments by currency and preserving the cutoff date.
inputs: The cutoff is September 30; the supplied transaction extract includes entries through October 3.
Eurovale Services invoice EUR-81 is EUR 9,000, with a posted EUR 500 credit and a EUR 2,000 partial payment, both dated September 28.
An additional EUR 1,500 payment against EUR-81 is dated October 2.
Brookfield Labs invoice USD-93 is USD 7,200, with a USD 1,200 partial payment dated September 30 and no recorded credits.
No exchange-rate schedule is supplied; keep EUR and USD totals separate and identify post-cutoff transactions without applying them to September balances.
The close accountant requests the table from the supplied extract and passes it to the controller, who uses it to support the month-end receivables review.

users.job_scope: Prepares cutoff-sensitive receivables schedules for month-end close.
Reviews month-end receivables and approves close adjustments.

dependencies.use: Provides the currency-separated table and post-cutoff transaction references for close review.

subtask: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an outstanding-balance table separating invoices, credits, and partial payments, and flag duplicate or missing records that need reconciliation before customer statements are issued.
inputs: A legacy-system extract and a replacement-system extract both contain Pinecrest Foods invoice INV-730 for $5,600 with the same customer ID and issue date.
Only the legacy extract contains posted credit memo CM-188 for $400 against INV-730.
Only the replacement extract contains receipt PAY-310 for $2,000 allocated to INV-730.
The replacement extract also lists Pinecrest invoice INV-744 for $1,900 and a $500 allocated partial payment; the legacy extract ends before that invoice's issue date.
Do not count the repeated INV-730 twice; retain source references and flag the cross-system credit and payment records for validation.

The systems accountant supplies extracts to the receivables lead; the lead passes the table and flagged records to the reconciliation clerk, who returns validated balances before the lead issues customer statements.

users.job_scope: Reviews customer balances and authorizes statement issuance.
Provides accounting extracts and explains migration record coverage.
Checks duplicate records and validates migrated transaction allocations.

dependencies.use: Supplies both system extracts and their coverage details.
Provides the table and flagged cross-system records for validation.
Returns validated balances for customer statement issuance.

subtask: Build a receivables forecast from billing schedules and historical collection intervals.

case_info.task_request: Build an eight-week receivables forecast from open invoices and scheduled subscription bills, using historical collection intervals by customer segment.
inputs: The forecast starts April 6, 2026; opening outstanding receivables total $186,000 across 42 invoices.
Example open invoices: INV-401, enterprise, $24,000, issued March 16; INV-402, small business, $3,600, issued March 30; neither has received a payment.
Scheduled subscription bills total $75,000 on April 15 and $82,000 on May 15; each batch is 60% enterprise and 40% small business.
Over the last six months, enterprise customers paid 50% of invoice value within 30 days, 35% within 45 days, and 15% within 60 days; small businesses paid 80% within 15 days and 20% within 30 days.
Use invoice issue dates rather than due dates to apply the collection intervals; exclude $9,000 of draft invoices awaiting approval.

users.job_scope: Maintains open invoice balances and prepares collection forecasts.
Uses expected customer receipts to plan weekly cash availability.

dependencies.use: Passes the receivables forecast for incorporation into the weekly cash plan.

subtask: Build a receivables forecast from billing schedules and historical collection intervals.

case_info.task_request: Forecast customer receipts for the next quarter from project billing milestones, distinguishing approved bills from milestones whose approval dates remain uncertain.
inputs: The forecast covers July through September 2026; opening receivables are $140,000.
Project P-21 has an approved $80,000 milestone scheduled for billing July 10 and a $60,000 milestone tentatively scheduled for August 20.
Project P-34 has a $45,000 milestone scheduled for billing July 31, subject to customer acceptance; the project manager expects acceptance between July 31 and August 21.
For the last 18 approved milestone invoices, customers paid 40% of value 30 days after billing, 40% after 45 days, and 20% after 60 days.
Opening invoice INV-711 has a remaining balance of $50,000 and was issued June 15; INV-712 has $90,000 outstanding and was issued June 30.
Treat tentative milestone dates as assumptions rather than confirmed billing events; project approval status will be updated before the forecast is finalized.

users.job_scope: Maintains project billing schedules and forecasts milestone collections.
Confirms milestone completion and customer acceptance timing.
Uses forecast receipts to assess quarterly funding needs.

dependencies.use: Provides milestone approval status and expected acceptance dates.
Passes the forecast with confirmed and assumption-dependent receipts distinguished.

subtask: Build a receivables forecast from billing schedules and historical collection intervals.

case_info.task_request: Build a six-week receivables forecast that separates routine collections, agreed installment payments, and disputed balances.
inputs: As of September 7, 2026, outstanding receivables are $210,000: $120,000 routine, $60,000 under a payment agreement, and $30,000 disputed.

goal: Assemble documents for a defined transaction workflow
subtask: Draft a cover explanation describing the contents of the assembled document set.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes
subtask: Classify incoming requests using supplied service categories and routing rules.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes
subtask: Classify incoming requests using supplied service categories and routing rules.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes

The published routing steps send rented-home repair complaints to housing enforcement, council-owned home repairs to the housing maintenance team, and owner-occupied repair inquiries to the advice service.
For rented-home complaints, the published steps require a copy of the landlord notification or a recorded explanation of why none is available before an inspection referral.
Three synthetic requests describe mold in a private rental with an email sent to the landlord 12 days ago, a leaking tap in a council-owned flat, and a damaged roof on an owner-occupied house.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes
subtask: Build an intake checklist from published process steps supplied with the task.

The published process separates ordinary certified-copy requests from record-correction requests. Corrections require the disputed entry, proposed replacement, and supporting evidence.
Published representative-request steps require signed authority from the record holder and identification from the representative; a request missing either item goes to the evidence-completion stage.

Synthetic request R21 seeks a birth certificate by post with all event details; R22 asks to correct a marriage-record surname but supplies no supporting evidence; R23 seeks a certificate through a representative with identification but no signed authority.

A registry team leader commissions the checklist for counter clerks. Clerks pass complete copy requests to the certificate officer and correction or incomplete-authority requests to the casework officer; no eligibility decisions have yet been made.

Collects applicant details and checks submitted materials.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes
subtask: Build an intake checklist from published process steps supplied with the task.

Published pavement-cafe steps additionally require a furniture layout, a clear pedestrian width of at least 1.8 metres, and evidence of public-liability insurance before assessment.

Published temporary street-event steps additionally require estimated attendance, event hours, and a traffic-management proposal if any carriageway closure is requested; applications must arrive at least 30 calendar days before the event.

Synthetic submission S14 proposes six cafe tables with a stated clear width of 1.6 metres; S15 proposes an 80-person street gathering in 45 days with no road closure; S16 proposes tables plus a one-day carriageway closure.

The licensing coordinator requests the checklist for the intake officer. The intake officer passes each selected route to the licensing assessor; the supplied publication does not explain how combined cafe-and-event submissions should be handled.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes
subtask: Build an intake checklist from published process steps supplied with the task.

Published routing steps send requests for the requester's own personal records to personal-data access, environmental information to environmental-information handling, and other recorded authority information to general information access.

The personal-data access steps require identity verification before records are released; the general information-access steps require a written request and correspondence address; environmental-information requests may be made orally.

Synthetic request I08 is labelled 'FOI' but seeks the requester's own benefit case notes; I09 is an oral request for river-sampling results from the last six months; I10 is an email seeking council stationery spending for one financial year.

The information governance manager commissions the checklist for the contact-centre adviser, who forwards intake records to the information rights officer. The checklist must not add identity checks to every route or decide whether any disclosure exemption applies.

goal: Sort requests into defined public-service processes

inputs: The fictional Southhaven Council's published missed-collection steps require the service address, scheduled collection date, waste type, and confirmation that the bin was presented by 7 a.m.; reports are accepted within two working days of the scheduled collection.

Published replacement-bin steps require the service address, bin type, and whether the bin is lost, damaged, or requested for a newly occupied property; damaged-bin requests also require a description of the damage.

Published illegal-dumping steps require the location and waste description, with photographs optional; intake staff must record whether waste is on public or private land, or mark land status as unknown.

Synthetic records W31 and W32 report the same missed recycling collection at 14 Example Lane on the same date; W33 requests a replacement cracked food-waste bin without describing the crack; W34 reports dumped bags beside a footpath with land status unknown.
The published steps require staff to check for an existing report before creating a new missed-collection case, but provide no equivalent duplicate rule for replacement bins or dumping reports.

The customer-services lead requests the checklist for service advisers. Advisers send missed-collection and replacement-bin records to the waste operations officer, and dumping records to the environmental services officer; collection dates and presentation times remain unverified.

Service delivery requires a confirmed booking; closure follows either delivery or cancellation, and cancellation may occur from any open request stage.

A synthetic sample contains 1,000 notice recipients: 620 have verified email addresses, 230 have no recorded email address, and 150 have unverified addresses.
Support flags identify 95 recipients requiring translated notices, 60 requiring accessible formats, and 140 with recorded digital-access difficulties; flags can overlap.
Both options preserve existing translation and accessible-format services; the digital-default option requires a clerk to arrange paper delivery when no verified email is available.
A pilot logged 40 returned letters among 400 paper notices and 18 failed deliveries among 300 digital notices; recipients were not randomly assigned.
The records officer sends the extract to the reform coordinator; the coordinator's table goes first to the equality adviser and then to the registrar for implementation planning.

users.job_scope: Compare administrative notice options and assemble impact evidence.

Check the treatment of overlapping communication-support needs.
Plan notice procedures and clerk responsibilities.

Forwards the reviewed table and coverage comments for implementation planning.

goal: Compare options for a stated policy problem

case_info.task_request: Prepare a distribution table of affected groups for the two floodplain building-rule options, separating existing properties from future applicants and marking effects that await mapping.
inputs: A district is comparing a ban on new residential construction in the designated floodplain with conditional approval requiring raised floor levels.
Synthetic parcel records identify 210 existing owner-occupied homes, 80 existing rented homes, 25 undeveloped residential parcels, and 12 commercial premises within the designated area.
Both options exempt existing buildings from new floor-level requirements; substantial-rebuild rules have not yet been drafted.
Six pending residential applications cover eight proposed homes; two applications are on parcels whose floodplain boundaries await survey confirmation.
An engineering estimate gives a $35,000–$55,000 raised-floor cost per new home but contains no estimates for commercial premises or substantial rebuilds.
The planning officer will send the table to the district policy chair, who will use the identified groups and gaps to scope the next evidence request.

users.job_scope: Compare building-rule options using parcel and application records.
