dependencies.use: Provides the distribution table to identify further mapping and cost evidence needed.

goal: Assess policy implementation using supplied records
subtask: Calculate implementation indicators from administrative records and supplied indicator definitions.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the housing-assistance implementation indicators from the supplied application records, applying the eligibility, deduplication, and timeliness definitions.
inputs: All records are synthetic; the reporting cohort is applications received in April 2025, with status recorded through May 31.
The intake extract contains 126 rows; eight rows are repeat submissions linked to existing application IDs, and six distinct applications were withdrawn before eligibility review.
Define review coverage as distinct nonwithdrawn applications with a completed eligibility review divided by all distinct nonwithdrawn applications in the cohort.

Define timely determination as eligible applications decided within 15 calendar days of receiving complete documentation divided by eligible applications with a decision; exclude cases still awaiting a decision.
Example records: H014 was complete April 4 and approved April 18; H027 was complete April 9 and denied April 28 as ineligible; H039 was complete April 22 and remained pending May 31.
The extract includes application ID, duplicate-of ID, withdrawal date, documentation-complete date, eligibility result, and decision date; preserve missing dates as unknown rather than imputing them.

users.job_scope: Calculates implementation measures for the municipal assistance policy.
Maintains application records and resolves duplicate or incomplete entries.
Uses implementation measures to plan administrative improvements.

dependencies.use: Supplies the intake extract and clarifies record-linking questions.
Provides calculated indicators and denominator qualifications for program planning.

goal: Assess policy implementation using supplied records
subtask: Calculate implementation indicators from administrative records and supplied indicator definitions.

case_info.task_request: Calculate both contract-count and expenditure-weighted compliance indicators for the local procurement policy using the supplied contract register.
inputs: The synthetic register covers 42 contracts awarded during the fiscal quarter; seven emergency exemptions are outside the policy's scope.
Define count compliance as in-scope contracts with documented local-supplier outreach divided by all in-scope contracts.

Define expenditure-weighted compliance as award value of in-scope contracts with documented outreach divided by total award value of all in-scope contracts; use original award value, not later amendments.
Example records: P101 has a $240,000 award, documented outreach, and no exemption; P102 has a $15,000 award, no outreach, and no exemption; P103 has a $90,000 award and an emergency exemption.
Three in-scope contracts have blank outreach fields; count them as not documented, and separately identify their count and award value.
The finance extract includes original award value and amended value in separate columns; all amounts are in the same currency.

users.job_scope: Assesses implementation of supplier-outreach requirements.
Maintains contract values and reconciles financial extracts.
Uses compliance measures to adjust purchasing procedures.

dependencies.use: Provides award-value fields and resolves value discrepancies.
Supplies count-based and value-weighted measures for procedure review.

goal: Assess policy implementation using supplied records
subtask: Calculate implementation indicators from administrative records and supplied indicator definitions.

case_info.task_request: Calculate accessibility-policy implementation indicators from the supplied facility records, distinguishing verified compliance from missing evidence.
inputs: The synthetic inventory contains 30 public service facilities subject to the accessibility policy as of June 30, 2025.
Define verification coverage as facilities with a completed inspection in the preceding 12 months divided by all 30 facilities.
Define verified compliance as inspected facilities passing every applicable mandatory item divided by facilities inspected in that period; items marked not applicable do not count as failures.
Example records: F03 has a May 12 inspection with 11 passes and one not-applicable item; F08 has a March 20 inspection with ten passes and two failures; F12 has no inspection date.
Five inspection records have blank mandatory-item results; exclude those facilities from the verified-compliance denominator and report them separately as incomplete evidence.

Remediation entries include action ID, facility ID, due date, and completion date; define on-time remediation as actions due during the quarter completed by their due dates divided by all actions due during the quarter.

users.job_scope: Calculates facility verification and remediation indicators.
Maintains inspection evidence and remediation records.
Uses verified indicators to prioritize facility improvements.
Coordinates correction of incomplete inspection evidence.

dependencies.use: Supplies facility inspections and remediation entries.
Provides verified indicators for improvement prioritization.
Identifies incomplete evidence requiring record correction.

goal: Assess policy implementation using supplied records
subtask: Calculate implementation indicators from administrative records and supplied indicator definitions.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the appeal-resolution indicators using the supplied event records, keeping filing-cohort measures separate from period-completion measures.
inputs: Synthetic appeal records cover filings from January through March 2025 and decision events through April 30; 80 appeals were filed during the first quarter.
Define cohort resolution as first-quarter filings receiving a final decision by April 30 divided by all first-quarter filings; withdrawn appeals remain in the denominator but are not final decisions.

Define period timeliness as appeals with final decisions issued during the first quarter within 30 calendar days of filing divided by all appeals with final decisions issued during that quarter, regardless of filing quarter.
Example records: A011 was filed December 18 and decided January 10; A032 was filed February 3 and decided March 12; A057 was filed March 21 and remained open April 30.
Each appeal can have hearing, interim-order, withdrawal, and final-decision events; only final-decision events establish resolution.
Two appeals have corrected final-decision events; use the event marked current, and flag appeals with more than one current final-decision event for clarification rather than selecting one.

users.job_scope: Measures implementation of appeal-processing standards.
Maintains case events and validates decision status.
Uses appeal indicators to review procedural implementation.

dependencies.use: Provides event records and clarifies conflicting decision entries.
Provides separately labeled cohort and completion-period indicators.

goal: Assess policy implementation using supplied records
subtask: Calculate implementation indicators from administrative records and supplied indicator definitions.

case_info.task_request: Calculate risk-stratified inspection coverage and observed correction indicators from the supplied licensing records without generalizing inspected-site results to all licensees.
inputs: The synthetic quarter-end register contains 120 active licensed food premises: 30 high-risk, 50 medium-risk, and 40 low-risk; risk category is fixed at quarter start.

Define inspection coverage within each risk category as distinct active premises receiving a completed inspection during the quarter divided by active premises in that category; repeat visits count once.
The visit log contains 48 completed visits and nine canceled appointments, with premises ID, visit date, completion status, and quarter-start risk category.
Example records: L004 is high-risk with completed visits April 8 and May 20; L019 is medium-risk with a canceled visit June 6; L083 is low-risk with a completed visit June 11.

Define observed timely correction as deficiencies due during the quarter and verified corrected by their due dates divided by all recorded deficiencies due during the quarter; unverified corrections do not enter the numerator.

Deficiency records include deficiency ID, premises ID, due date, claimed-correction date, and verification date; results describe recorded deficiencies at inspected premises, not compliance across the full register.

users.job_scope: Calculates inspection coverage and recorded correction measures.
Maintains visit outcomes and verifies deficiency corrections.
Uses risk-stratified measures to plan future inspection allocation.

dependencies.use: Supplies visit and deficiency records with verification status.
Provides coverage and observed correction indicators with scope limitations.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an example table comparing the current and proposed vendor-preference rules, highlighting the policy change for committee members and procurement staff.
inputs: Under the fictional current rule, an eligible local vendor's bid receives a 5% reduction for evaluation only; under the proposal, the reduction is 8%.
Local eligibility requires both a registered office in the municipality and at least 50% of employees working there; the lowest evaluated bid wins.
Vendor A bids $100,000, has a municipal registered office, and has 60% local employees; vendor B bids $94,000 and has no municipal office.
Vendor C bids $97,000, has a municipal registered office, and has 40% local employees; all three bids satisfy the technical requirements.
The preference changes evaluation amounts only, not contract prices; the proposal has not been adopted.
Use the same bids in both comparisons and keep current provisions distinct from proposed provisions.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an example table illustrating the supplied administrative-appeal deadline rules, emphasizing date counting for reception staff and appellants.
inputs: The fictional rule allows an appeal within 10 calendar days after notice delivery; the delivery day is excluded.
If the tenth day falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a listed agency holiday, the deadline moves to the next day that is neither a weekend nor a listed holiday.
Listed agency holidays for these examples are Monday, June 15, 2026, and Friday, July 3, 2026; no other holidays apply.
Record A was delivered June 1, 2026, with an appeal received June 11; record B was delivered June 3, 2026, with an appeal received June 16.
Record C was delivered June 23, 2026, with an appeal received July 6; all dates and records are synthetic.
Use recorded receipt dates without time-of-day cutoffs; extensions and delivery disputes are outside the supplied rules.

case_info.task_request: Prepare an example table applying the supplied sidewalk-café permit provisions, showing which examples are clear and which require policy clarification.
inputs: The fictional permit rule requires at least 1.8 metres of unobstructed pedestrian clearance and limits seating to one chair per 1.2 square metres of licensed café area, rounded down.
Applications meeting both limits use routine review; applications below the clearance minimum require accessibility review and cannot be treated as routinely compliant.
Site A proposes 10 chairs in 12 square metres with 1.9 metres of clearance; site B proposes 13 chairs in 15 square metres with 2.0 metres of clearance.
Site C proposes 8 chairs in 12 square metres with 1.7 metres of clearance; site D proposes 6 chairs in 8 square metres and reports clearance varying from 1.75 to 1.95 metres.
The supplied provisions do not specify how variable clearance is measured; a measurement-method clarification is pending.
Separate numerical seating limits from review routing, and do not invent a measurement rule for site D.

subtask: Calculate composite scores using supplied item mappings and scoring rules.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the weighted service-experience composite, preserving its domain scores and identifying records that cannot be scored.
inputs: The synthetic resident survey extract contains 85 records with respondent_id, A1–A2, C1–C2, and T1–T2.
Map access to A1–A2, clarity to C1–C2, and trust to T1–T2; all items use a 1–7 scale with higher values favorable and no reverse scoring.
For each domain, require both items and transform their mean to a 0–100 score using 100 × (mean − 1) / 6.
The overall composite is 0.50 × access + 0.30 × clarity + 0.20 × trust; require all three domains and do not redistribute weights.
Blank and code 98 mean missing; example records are S021: A1=6, A2=5, C1=4, C2=5, T1=6, T2=7; S022: A1=3, A2=98, C1=4, C2=4, T1=5, T2=5.
Retain full precision during calculation and round displayed domain and overall scores to one decimal place.

case_info.task_request: Calculate the standardized civic-engagement composite from the supplied reference parameters, keeping component scores for the analyst.
inputs: The synthetic civic survey extract contains 200 respondents with items V1–V2 and D1–D2 plus monthly participation count P.
Map voice to the mean of V1 and V2 and deliberation to the mean of D1 and D2; these four items use a 1–5 scale with no reverse scoring.
Standardize voice using reference mean 3.2 and SD 0.8, deliberation using mean 3.5 and SD 0.6, and P using mean 2.0 and SD 1.5; use z=(value−reference mean)/reference SD.
The composite is the equal-weight mean of the three standardized components; use the supplied reference parameters rather than estimating new ones from this extract.
Require all five inputs; blanks and code −9 are missing, and P must be an integer from 0 to 20. Flag invalid values and leave affected composites missing.

Example records are I041: USED=1, H1=1, H2=0, H3=1, H4=0; I042: USED=0 with all H items blank; I043: USED=1, H1=0, H2=8, H3=0, H4=1.

case_info.task_request: Compare engagement and expressed concerns for the two flood-preparedness video versions across both publication periods without treating comment sentiment as representative of all viewers.
inputs: Synthetic county outreach records cover August 4–10 and August 18–24; a demonstration video and a resident-story video appeared in both periods.
First period: demonstration had 12,000 starts, 4,800 completions, and 60 comments; resident story had 10,000 starts, 5,000 completions, and 90 comments.
Second period: demonstration had 15,000 starts, 5,250 completions, and 75 comments; resident story had 11,000 starts, 5,720 completions, and 110 comments.

Moderation tags across both periods: demonstration comments included 48 cost concerns and 22 requests for supply lists; resident-story comments included 65 cost concerns and 50 requests for supply lists; tags can overlap.
A local flood anniversary fell in the second period; example comments included 'I rent, so can I install this?' and 'Please post a printable supply list.'
The campaign manager shares the comparison separately with the preparedness educator for content revisions and the accessibility specialist for review of requests for alternative formats.

users.job_scope: Schedules preparedness communication and reviews audience engagement.
Develops practical household preparedness guidance.
Reviews public materials for accessible formats and usability.

dependencies.use: Uses the requested comparison to revise practical guidance and address expressed concerns.
Uses the requested comparison to review requests for printable or alternative formats.

goal: Interpret audience responses and communication results
subtask: Compare audience responses across content versions and publication periods.

case_info.task_request: Compare responses to the short and detailed library-hours notices across the pilot and wider publication periods, identifying which comparisons require data checks before reuse.
inputs: Synthetic library records cover a September 2–8 pilot at two branches and a September 16–22 rollout at six branches.
The short notice listed changed hours; the detailed notice also explained staffing arrangements and alternative pickup options.
Pilot exports show short: 1,200 deliveries, 96 link clicks, 12 replies; detailed: 1,100 deliveries, 121 link clicks, 20 replies.
Rollout exports show short: 4,800 deliveries, 336 link clicks, 44 replies; detailed: 4,600 deliveries, 414 link clicks, 63 replies.
Pilot clicks are labeled unique recipients, but rollout clicks are labeled total events; nine rollout replies appear twice with matching timestamps and text.
The library communications officer requests checks from the mailing-list administrator, then passes the checked comparison to the service manager, who uses it to brief branch supervisors.

users.job_scope: Publishes service notices and compares patron responses.
Maintains mailing exports and verifies delivery, click, and reply definitions.
Coordinates branch services and prepares supervisors for patron questions.

dependencies.use: Uses the requested comparison to check click definitions and potentially duplicated replies.
Returns verified metric definitions and corrected records for the comparison.
Supplies the checked comparison for briefing branch supervisors.

case_info.task_request: Build a feedback table linking recurring library-hours questions to existing information resources, keeping branch-specific questions separate.
inputs: A synthetic set contains 84 comments from a library-service survey and 26 questions received at branch desks.
Example records include 'Is North Branch open on Sundays?' and 'Can I return books after the building closes?'
The supplied resource inventory includes a branch-hours webpage, an after-hours returns guide, and a holiday-closure calendar.
North Branch and Riverside Branch have different weekend hours; the hours webpage lists both separately.
Include question wording, source channel, recurrence count, resource title, and resource section; mark questions without a matching resource.

users.job_scope: Collects patron feedback and requests links to published service information.
Checks branch-specific details and uses the table to prepare staff responses.
Uses confirmed resource gaps to plan webpage updates.

dependencies.use: Passes the feedback table for branch-detail checks and staff-response preparation.
Passes checked entries and unmatched questions for webpage-update planning.

subtask: Build a feedback table linking recurring questions to existing information resources.

case_info.task_request: Build a feedback table linking recurring vaccination-clinic questions to existing resources, distinguishing English and Spanish feedback without combining uncertain translations.
inputs: The supplied synthetic feedback contains 48 English comments and 31 Spanish comments from community information sessions.
Example records include 'Do I need insurance?' and '¿Puedo ir sin cita?'
Existing resources are an English clinic FAQ, a Spanish clinic FAQ, and a bilingual location-and-hours sheet.
Both FAQs have numbered sections, but their section numbering differs; the Spanish FAQ was revised two months before the English version.
Six Spanish comments have provisional translations supplied by outreach staff and marked 'review pending.'
Keep source language and translation-review status visible, and flag resource matches that require bilingual review.

users.job_scope: Organizes community-session feedback and requests resource mapping.
Checks translated questions and language-specific resource matches.
Uses reviewed links to prepare public-facing clinic responses.

dependencies.use: Sends the table for review of provisional translations and bilingual matches.
Provides reviewed question-resource links for clinic-response preparation.

subtask: Build a feedback table linking recurring questions to existing information resources.

case_info.task_request: Build a feedback table linking recurring bus-route consultation questions to existing resources, preserving differences between response channels and separating questions from preferences.
inputs: Synthetic consultation records comprise 120 online submissions, 35 meeting question cards, and 18 telephone notes.
Example records include 'Will Route 8 still stop at the hospital?', 'Keep the hospital stop,' and 'When would the change start?'
The resource pack contains proposed route maps, a consultation timeline, and an accessibility FAQ, each with a supplied reference ID.
The maps show proposed stops rather than approved routes; no final implementation date has been published.
Some telephone notes summarize several callers and lack individual counts; report their frequency as unknown rather than estimating it.
Retain channel-level counts and use the supplied reference IDs for resource links.

users.job_scope: Organizes consultation responses and requests question-resource mapping.
Checks whether mapped resources accurately describe the proposal.
Uses checked links to prepare consultation follow-up information.

dependencies.use: Passes the table for checks against proposed route details.
Supplies checked links and unresolved questions for public follow-up.

subtask: Build a feedback table linking recurring questions to existing information resources.

case_info.task_request: Build a feedback table linking recurring recycling-campaign questions to existing resources, showing which campaign messages prompted them and flagging conflicting guidance.
inputs: A synthetic campaign export contains 66 questions tagged to three messages: bin labels, food-container preparation, and collection-day changes.
Example records include 'Do yogurt pots need washing?' and 'Does the new label mean black plastic is accepted?'
Available resources are a materials lookup page, a printable sorting leaflet, and a collection-calendar webpage.
The lookup page was updated in April; the supplied leaflet is dated January and gives different guidance for black plastic.
The export includes 12 repeated submissions with matching synthetic respondent IDs and identical text.
Show raw and deduplicated recurrence counts, preserve message tags, and do not choose between conflicting resource statements.

users.job_scope: Reviews campaign responses and requests a traceable resource-mapping table.
Resolves conflicts between published sorting instructions.
Uses question patterns and confirmed guidance to revise campaign wording.

dependencies.use: Sends flagged resource conflicts for policy clarification.
Shares question counts and campaign-message tags for wording review.
Provides confirmed sorting guidance before revised wording is prepared.

subtask: Build a feedback table linking recurring questions to existing information resources.

case_info.task_request: Build a feedback table linking recurring housing-grant webinar questions to existing resources, distinguishing full, partial, and missing coverage without drafting new answers.
inputs: The supplied synthetic material includes 52 webinar chat questions and 14 follow-up emails, all with personal identifiers removed.
Example records include 'Can tenants apply?', 'What proof of income is needed?', and 'Can two households share one application?'
Resources comprise an eligibility guide, an application checklist, and a webinar transcript with timestamps.
The transcript includes audience questions as well as presenter responses; an unanswered audience question is not an information resource.
The eligibility guide covers owner-occupiers, while the checklist lists income evidence but does not address shared applications.
Record the supporting section or timestamp and coverage status; eligibility interpretations remain for the programme officer to review.

users.job_scope: Collects webinar feedback and requests links to existing grant information.
Reviews eligibility-related matches and determines which gaps need clarification.
Uses reviewed resources when responding to applicant inquiries.

dependencies.use: Passes the table for coverage checks and eligibility review.
Shares approved resource matches and questions still awaiting clarification.

case_info.task_request: Prepare a content revision plan for our recycling guidance using the supplied feedback, prioritizing correct sorting over page visits.
inputs: Synthetic pilot results: 240 residents viewed the guidance; 68 completed a sorting quiz, and 29 correctly classified greasy pizza boxes.
Example feedback: 'The picture shows a whole pizza box, but the text says only clean cardboard.'
The current page lists 14 accepted materials before explaining contamination rules.
The communication goal is to raise correct sorting responses to 75% in the next pilot; the page must remain under 600 words.
The waste educator supplies sorting rules to the communications coordinator, who passes the revision plan to the web editor for implementation.

users.job_scope: Coordinates resident guidance and requests content revisions.
Confirms local sorting rules and explains common disposal mistakes.
Updates public guidance pages and arranges the next comprehension test.

dependencies.use: Provides verified sorting rules and pilot feedback for the revision request.
Passes the revision plan for page changes and a follow-up comprehension test.

subtask: Prepare a content revision plan from supplied feedback and communication goals.

case_info.task_request: Prepare a content revision plan for the library enrollment campaign, emphasizing language accessibility and identifying feedback gaps before rewriting.
inputs: Synthetic campaign records: English posts received 1,800 impressions and 54 application starts; Spanish posts received 900 impressions and 11 starts.
Feedback came from 18 English-speaking respondents and three Spanish-speaking respondents; no preferred-language data were collected from applicants.
Example comments: 'Does free membership require citizenship?' and 'Can I apply without a utility bill?'
The goal is to help eligible residents understand enrollment requirements; approved policy allows several address-verification alternatives.
The outreach librarian passes the plan to a bilingual reviewer for terminology checks and to a community liaison for additional feedback recruitment.

users.job_scope: Coordinates enrollment communication and maintains approved eligibility information.
Checks English and Spanish content for equivalent meaning and accessible wording.
Recruits residents for feedback sessions through neighborhood organizations.

dependencies.use: Shares the revision plan for language and terminology review.
Shares identified feedback gaps to guide participant recruitment.

subtask: Prepare a content revision plan from supplied feedback and communication goals.

case_info.task_request: Prepare a content revision plan for the park redesign consultation, focusing on perceived neutrality and clearly distinguishing settled decisions from open questions.
inputs: Synthetic consultation feedback includes 46 written responses: 19 mention a predetermined outcome, 12 ask about tree removal, and eight request accessible seating.
The current introduction says, 'Help us deliver the exciting new plaza,' while the survey asks whether residents prefer a plaza or a planted lawn.
The approved budget is $420,000; layout and seating remain open, but the accessible entrance location is fixed.
Two neighborhood groups submitted contrasting preferences; their submissions do not report membership counts or sampling methods.
The engagement officer receives decision boundaries from the landscape planner and sends the revision plan to the meeting facilitator for use in public sessions.

users.job_scope: Coordinates consultation language and interprets resident feedback.
Defines design options, budget limits, and decisions that are already fixed.
Uses approved consultation content to introduce options and collect public responses.

dependencies.use: Supplies confirmed decision boundaries and feasible design options.
Passes the revision plan to align session introductions and discussion prompts.

case_info.task_request: Prepare a content revision plan for the vaccination appointment messages, emphasizing completion barriers and keeping all clinical claims within the approved wording.
inputs: Synthetic message results: 1,200 texts were delivered, 216 booking links were opened, and 63 appointments were completed within seven days.
Among 24 callback records, nine callers asked about cost, seven asked about evening appointments, and five reported that the link opened a general clinic homepage.
Current text: 'Protect your community. Book now.' It does not mention that appointments are free or that Tuesday sessions run until 8 p.m.
The communication goal is appointment completion; texts are limited to 160 characters, and clinical claims require approval before publication.
The clinic communications officer passes proposed revisions to the clinical reviewer, who forwards cleared wording to the scheduling coordinator.

users.job_scope: Reviews campaign responses and coordinates appointment-message revisions.
Checks health statements against approved clinical wording.
Publishes cleared messages and verifies appointment links and session details.

dependencies.use: Submits the revision plan and proposed wording for clinical clearance.
Forwards cleared wording and implementation requirements for scheduling communication.

goal: Interpret audience responses and communication results
subtask: Prepare a content revision plan from supplied feedback and communication goals.

case_info.task_request: Prepare a content revision plan for the bus timetable change campaign, separating channel-specific revisions from questions that need further testing.
inputs: Synthetic results: the email reached 3,400 subscribers with 680 timetable downloads; printed notices were placed at 22 stops, with no exposure count available.
A convenience sample of 35 riders included 21 who recalled the new start date and 10 who correctly identified the replacement stop for Route 6.
Example feedback: 'The email says next Monday, but the poster says June 10'; both refer to the same effective date.
The replacement-stop map uses color alone to distinguish old and new stops; the printed notice must fit an A4 sheet.
The goal is correct travel planning rather than downloads; route information is confirmed, but revised wording and map symbols have not been tested.
The passenger information manager receives feedback records from the research officer and sends the plan to the designer for email, poster, and map revisions.

users.job_scope: Coordinates public timetable information and sets communication goals.
Collects rider feedback and documents sampling and measurement limits.
Revises passenger messages and maps across digital and printed channels.

dependencies.use: Supplies feedback records and measurement limitations for revision planning.
Passes channel-specific revision requirements and items needing prototype testing.
